title_en: Tones First — the fast track starts here
subtitle: Four tones, one syllable, instant Chinese
description: The one-hour foundation for speaking Mandarin: the four tones plus neutral, tone-pair drills, the tricky zh/ch/sh/r sounds and your first sentences — with English and Khmer support and native audio on every line.

spine.title: The route · your first hour
spine.note: Hear the four tones on one syllable, glue them into real pairs, fix the sounds English doesn't have, then speak full sentences.

explain.title: The big picture
explain.why: Mandarin uses pitch to tell words apart, so tones are not decoration — they ARE the word. Learn the four contours on one syllable and you can pronounce any pinyin you ever meet.

tiles.en: The mark above the vowel is the tone
Tone 1: high and flat, like a held note
Tone 3: dips low, the slowest one

cards.alt: Four contour lines over the syllable ma with a horse icon
cards.ko: 妈 mā · 麻 má · 马 mǎ · 骂 mà — one syllable, four different words.
cards.en: mā mother · má hemp · mǎ horse · mà to scold. The tone changes the word.
cards.km: ម៉ា ទាំងបួនសូរ៖ mā ម្ដាយ · má ស្ពៃ · mǎ សេះ · mà ចំហាល។

cards.alt: A small light feather over a flat line
cards.ko: 吗 ma 是轻声：又短又轻。
cards.en: The neutral tone (ma) is short and light — no mark above the vowel.
cards.km: សូរខ្សោយ ma ខ្លី និងស្រាល។

cards.alt: Two linked tiles showing tone contours 3+3 and 4+4
cards.ko: 两个第三声连在一起，第一个读第二声：你好 → ní hǎo。
cards.en: When two third tones meet, the first becomes a second: 你好 is read 'ní hǎo'.
cards.km: បើសូរទី៣ ពីរជួបគ្នា សូរទីមួយ អានជាសូរទី២។

cards.alt: A side-view mouth with the tongue curled up
cards.en: For zh, ch, sh and r curl the tip of your tongue up toward the roof of your mouth.
cards.km: សម្រាប់ zh ch sh r ងូញអណ្តាតឡើងលើ។

cards.alt: Three word blocks snapping together: subject, verb, object
cards.ko: 中文句子和英语一样：主语 + 动词 + 宾语，动词不变。
cards.en: Chinese word order is Subject + Verb + Object like English — and verbs never change form.
cards.km: ប្រយោគចិន៖ មេរៀន + កិរិយាសព្ទ + វត្ថុ ដូចភាសាអង់គ្លេស ហើយកិរិយាសព្ទមិនប្តូរទេ។

cards.alt: A statement tile with a question-mark chip labelled 吗 snapping on the end
cards.ko: 陈述句 + 吗 = 一般疑问句：你喜欢咖啡 → 你喜欢咖啡吗？
cards.en: Add 吗 to the end of any statement and it becomes a yes/no question.
cards.km: ដាក់ ma នៅចុងប្រយោគ ក្លាយជាសំណួរ បាទ/ចាស។

qa_note: Recall the answer in your head first, then tap to check and listen.

items.q: 可以不学声调，只学拼音吗？
items.qen: Can I skip tones and just learn pinyin?
items.a: 不行。妈、马不一样；声调错了，意思就变了。
items.aen: No. mā (mother) and mǎ (horse) are different words — wrong tone, wrong meaning.
items.akm: មិនបានទេ។ mā ម្ដាយ និង mǎ សេះ ជាពាក្យខុសគ្នា។
items.why: Tones are part of the word itself, like a letter. Learners who skip them speak years without being understood.

items.q: 声调说错了，别人听得懂吗？
items.qen: If I get a tone wrong, will people understand me?
items.a: 大多数时候能听懂。别怕，先开口，慢慢就准了。
items.aen: Usually yes — context carries you. Speak first; accuracy comes with practice.
items.akm: ភាគច្រើន គេយល់។ កុំខ្លាច គ្រាន់តែនិយាយមុន។
items.why: Native listeners use context constantly. Perfection is not the gate to conversation — speaking is.

items.q: 要先会汉字才能开口说吗？
items.qen: Do I need characters before I can speak?
items.a: 不用。口语用拼音就能开始，汉字可以慢慢来。
items.aen: No. For speaking, pinyin is enough to start; learn characters slowly in parallel.
items.akm: មិនចាំបាច់ទេ។ សម្រាប់និយាយ pinyin គ្រប់គ្រាន់ដើម្បីចាប់ផ្តើម។
items.why: The fast track is sound-first: pinyin + tones + phrases. Characters pay off later, for reading.

items.qen: How long per day is the fastest progress?
items.a: 每天十五分钟，比一周一次两小时有效。
items.aen: Fifteen focused minutes every day beats two hours once a week.
items.akm: ប្រាំមួយនាទីរាល់ថ្ងៃ ល្អជាងពីរម៉ោងមួយសប្តាហ៍។

items.a: 对英语母语者，第二声和第三声最容易混。多听对比。
items.aen: For English speakers, tones 2 and 3 blur together most. Drill them as minimal pairs.
items.akm: សម្រាប់អ្នកនិយាយអង់គ្លេស សូរទី២ និងទី៣ ពិបាកជាងគេ។

items.km: សូមនិយាយយឺតៗបន្តិច។
ពាក្យនេះ មានន័យថាអ្វី?
ខ្ញុំ និយាយ មិនទាន់ បាន ទេ។

qa.title: Patterns · the grammar you need today

items.qen: Pattern: Subject + Verb + Object — 'I like coffee.'
items.a: 他喜欢茶。我们学习中文。
items.aen: He likes tea. We study Chinese. The verb never changes.
items.akm: គាត់ ចូលចិត្ត តែ។ យើង រៀន ភាសាចិន។

items.a: 你喜欢茶吗？——喜欢 / 不喜欢。
items.aen: Do you like tea? — Yes (like) / No (don't like). Answer with the verb itself.
items.akm: តើ អ្នក ចូលចិត្ត តែ ទេ? — ចូលចិត្ត / មិន ចូលចិត្ត។

items.qen: Pattern: put 不 before the verb to say no.
items.aen: I'm not a teacher. He doesn't go. 不 sits right before the verb.
items.akm: ខ្ញុំ មិន មែន គ្រូ ទេ។ គាត់ មិន ទៅ ទេ។
